expectations.text: S1: flags that api_redeem swallows exceptions so redeeming an unknown code appears to succeed (app/api.py, try/except around STORE.discounts[code]).

The resulting `KeyError` on `STORE.discounts[code]` is swallowed by `except Exception: pass`." Evidence: "`api_redeem({\"code\": \"NOPE\"})` returned `{'redeemed': True}`".

expectations.text: S2: flags that users.create_user dropped email lowercasing/normalization, citing docs/invariants.md §1 or util.normalize_email.

expectations.text: S3: flags that discount percent is never validated at the API boundary even though the PR description claims it is (validate_percent defined but uncalled).
expectations.evidence: C1 "Discount percent is never validated, so any percent is accepted": "`validate_percent` exists in the engine package but nothing calls it... expectations.text: S4: flags the check-then-act race on uses vs max_uses in api_redeem allowing over-redemption under concurrency.
expectations.evidence: No mention of concurrency or a race anywhere in the report (grep for race/concurren/atomic hits only one line). H1 flags over-redemption via a different mechanism (billing.charge never reads or increments uses) and says "The two steps are also never atomic, so a redeem followed by a failed charge burns a use for nothing", which is redeem-vs-charge sequencing, not two concurrent redeems both passing `uses < max_uses`. The seeded race was not surfaced.

Surfaced as a Suggestion rather than an Issue, with a measured no-divergence claim I reproduced (0 divergences over 1..199,999).

First What sentences are concrete mechanisms, e.g. C1 "`api_create_discount` stores `int(payload[\"percent\"])` with no range check.", C3 "`create_user` no longer lowercases the email.", H2 "The endpoint strips a leading `-` and negates the parsed value, which defeats the one rule `parse_money` enforces." notes: The two misses are informative. S4 is arguably mis-targeted for this fixture: billing.charge never reads uses at all, so the reviewer found the larger hole (unbounded reuse, confirmed by probe) and the concurrency race on a counter nothing enforces became moot. Consider accepting either framing, or rewording S4 to 'over-redemption of max_uses' with the race as one acceptable mechanism. S6 is a genuine trip: the commit body says 'finance signed off', yet M3 asks for the sign-off and Q1 asks whether finance intended it. That is exactly the intent-reading failure the trap targets, though a softer one than calling the value wrong, so the assertion could distinguish 'flags as wrong' (hard fail) from 'flags as unbundled scope' if the author considers the latter acceptable. Two outcomes no assertion covers: the report found the cross-file support.lookup TypeError (C2) that the README reserves for eval 3, and the verifier/worktree hiccup recorded under Known limitations, both worth a bonus or robustness check. S5 passed as a Suggestion rather than an Issue; the assertion says 'surfaces', which is fine, but if the author wants it rated it should say so.
